reason: Driven at 1440x960, state=publish, every visible text node harvested with its box. The positions do not support the reading, and the panel has already ruled on these exact three words twice. (1) ALREADY ADJUDICATED. The round-7 CONFIRMED verdict taste--publish-is-not-a-ceremony is the finding that produced this headline, and its sharpened fix says verbatim: "Headline the fact ('Mara & Finn have had this since 15 July.'), make Copy the link the primary act, and drop 'Ready to send. The link is below.' - it contradicts the card beside it, which already says 'when this was sent'. Keep 'Sending comes next'." The build did exactly that: render-b.js:1183 conditionalises the announcement, 1471 conditionalises the headline, 1500 keeps the label. The finding calls the surviving label an oversight - "the inert label was left unconditional" - when it is the one string the ratifying verdict named and told the build to keep, in the same sentence that killed the other. Round 5's verdict publish-says-three-things refused a rewrite here for the same reason, naming this label as the string that "agrees that sending is still the owner's act". (2) FACTUALLY WRONG ABOUT THE FRAME. It is not "three hundred pixels below" and not "under the primary button". Measured: h2.b-pressTitle top y=350; span.b-inert y=622, x=688 - 272px down and INLINE TO THE RIGHT of the Copy the link button (y=620, x=575), on the same row, with three blocks (body copy, link field, action row) between. It is 11px mono, uppercase, tracked, at 62% ink against a 48px 600 headline. The rhetorical charge - "contradicts itself in two type sizes" - depends on it reading as prose beneath the CTA; it reads as a step caption pinned to the CTA. (3) THE REGISTERS ARE NOT THE SAME SPEAKER. b.css:651 declares the class's meaning: "Not built is not a button. A focusable promise is worse than silence." .b-inert is a two-use vocabulary in this artifact - "Nothing to preview yet" (render-b.js:1301) and "Sending comes next" - and both mean the same thing: a capability the product does not perform for you. It is not a tense claim about this plan's history; it is the brief's named honesty device, that the product does not send. Nothing in it asserts a first send. The owner is on this surface because they pressed a door that on the published branch reads "Get the link" (render-b.js:1220) - and after copying a link that already went to the couple, sending it on to a family or the venue is literally the next act. (4) THE FIX WOULD MAKE IT WORSE, AND DELETES THE ADMISSION. fixture.js:182 hardcodes publication.state "published" and it is the single source for every frame, so `render only when state !== "published"` is not a gate, it is a deletion: the unpublished branch is unreachable and renders in no gradeable state. Round 5's refuter made this exact reachability point about this exact surface. Grep confirms "Sending comes next" is the ONLY remaining string in the artifact that says the product does not send - 1181/1183 are the retired announcement, 1473 is the dead unpublished headline. Remove it and the publish screen's whole instruction to the owner is a primary button and a revoke note: the audience the brief names, who has never used a project-management tool, is handed a copied string and told nothing about what to do with it. That trades an arguable 11px tense reading for a real dead end on the surface that hands the plan over.
sharpenedFix: If the seat still wants the two lines further apart in the reader's ear after the above, the change is one word inside the existing device, not a gate: "Sending comes next" -> "You do the sending" or "Sending is yours", which keeps .b-inert's declared meaning (a thing the product does not do), keeps the admission the brief calls load-bearing and the round-7 verdict told the build to keep, and drops the only word - "next" - that carries any sequence at all. No branch, no deletion, no unreachable code path. Even this is a taste trim, not a defect: at 11px mono 62% inline beside the button, the label is read as a caption on the act, not as a claim about 15 July.
